separable: inseparable — *sneeze at the offer*, never ✗ *sneeze the offer at*. In practice it is almost always negative: *nothing to sneeze at*, *not to be sneezed at*.
gloss: To treat something as too small or unimportant to be worth having.
examples: A ten percent raise is nothing to *sneeze at*.
Nobody *sneezed at* the offer once they saw the numbers.
He spent two years *sneezing at* jobs that paid less than six figures.

separable: separable — *sock away money*, *sock money away*, *sock it away*; a pronoun has to sit in the middle, never ✗ *sock away it*.
gloss: To save money steadily and keep it somewhere safe for the future.
examples: They *sock away* three hundred dollars every month.
By forty she had *socked away* enough to stop worrying.
He *socks* a little *away* out of every paycheck.

ru: впитывать, впитать; вымакивать, вымакать (хлебом); собирать, собрать (жидкость)
separable: separable — *sop up the gravy*, *sop the gravy up*, *sop it up*; never ✗ *sop up it*. The p doubles: *sopped*, *sopping*.
gloss: To soak up a liquid with bread, a cloth, or a sponge.
examples: He *sopped up* the last of the gravy with a biscuit.
Use a paper towel to *sop up* the spill.
She was *sopping* the grease *up* with an old rag.

separable: separable — *soup up the engine*, *soup the engine up*, *soup it up*; never ✗ *soup up it*. The participle is a common adjective: *a souped-up Civic*.
gloss: To make an engine or a machine more powerful than it was built to be.
examples: He *souped up* an old Civic in his father's garage.
They *soup up* the delivery vans so they can keep up on the highway.
The shop is *souping* the motor *up* for Saturday's race.

ru: настраивать, настроить против; складываться, сложиться не в пользу (кого-л.)
separable: always split — what gets stacked goes in the middle: *stack the odds against him*, never ✗ *stack against him the odds*. The passive is commonest of all: *the odds are stacked against us*.
gloss: To arrange things so that someone is at a disadvantage from the start.
examples: The lending rules were *stacked against* first-time buyers.
A late start and bad weather *stacked* everything *against* the climbers.
Every change to the funding formula keeps *stacking* the deck *against* rural schools.

separable: no object of its own — what you start in on follows *on*: *start in on the leftovers*, *start in on me about the car*.
gloss: To begin something with a lot of energy, especially criticizing someone or eating.
examples: Don't *start in* on me — I already apologized.
She *started in* on her brother the moment he walked through the door.
He was *starting in* on a second plate before anyone else sat down.

ru: нажимать, нажать (на педаль); прибавлять, прибавить газу; поторапливаться
separable: inseparable — what you press follows the particle: *step on the gas*, *step on the brake*, never ✗ *step the brake on*. The fixed phrase *step on it* means hurry.
gloss: To press a pedal down with your foot, especially to make a car go faster.
examples: *Step on it* — the flight leaves in forty minutes.
He *stepped on* the gas and the truck jumped forward.
She kept *stepping on* the brake all the way down the hill.

separable: inseparable — the person follows the particle: *step on people*, never ✗ *step people on*.
gloss: To treat people badly or ignore their feelings in order to get what you want.
examples: He *stepped on* a lot of people on his way to that corner office.
Managers who *step on* their staff don't keep them long.
You can get promoted here without *stepping on* anyone.

separable: separable — *suck in your stomach*, *suck your stomach in*, *suck it in*; never ✗ *suck in it*.
gloss: To pull air, or a part of your body, inward.
examples: He *sucked in* a long breath before he answered.
*Suck* your gut *in* and the pants will button.
She was *sucking in* air through her teeth the whole time.

ru: втягивать, втянуть (в историю); обманывать, обмануть, облапошить
separable: separable — *suck in new investors*, *suck him in*; with a pronoun it must split, never ✗ *suck in him*. Very often passive: *I got sucked in*.
gloss: To draw someone into a situation or a scam they never meant to join.
examples: The free trial *sucked in* thousands of subscribers.
Don't let those ads *suck* you *in*.
He got *sucked in* by a guy selling fake playoff tickets.

ru: убывать, убыть; идти на убыль; сходить на нет
separable: no object — intransitive: *sales tailed off*. Nothing can sit between the two words.
gloss: To become gradually smaller or weaker until it nearly stops.
examples: Ticket sales *tailed off* right after the holidays.
Donations always *tail off* in February.
Applications have been *tailing off* since the fee went up.

separable: inseparable — *talk about the budget*, never ✗ *talk the budget about*. English needs the *about*: ✗ *talk the problem*, and the same trap in reverse with *discuss*, which takes no preposition: *discuss the budget*.
gloss: To say things to someone on a particular subject.
examples: Can we *talk about* this tomorrow?
They *talked about* moving to Denver for the better part of an hour.
Everyone at work is *talking about* the merger.

ru: говорить, не слушая собеседника; вещать; отчитывать
separable: inseparable — the person follows the particle: *talk at me*, never ✗ *talk me at*. Compare *talk to*, which is a two-way conversation.
gloss: To speak to someone without listening to anything they say back.
examples: He *talks at* you for an hour and calls it a meeting.
The consultant *talked at* us for ninety minutes straight.
I'm tired of being *talked at* in these trainings.

separable: inseparable in this sense, and it needs *to*: *talk down to the audience*, never ✗ *talk the audience down to*.
gloss: To speak to someone as though they were less intelligent than you.
examples: Don't *talk down to* me — I read the same report you did.
The specialist *talked down to* her for the whole visit.
Nobody learns much from a teacher who is always *talking down to* the class.

separable: separable — *talk down the gunman*, *talk the gunman down*; with a pronoun it must split: *talk her down*, never ✗ *talk down her*.
gloss: To calm someone or persuade them to give up a dangerous plan by talking to them.
examples: A negotiator *talked* the man *down* from the bridge.
Her sister can usually *talk* her *down* when she starts panicking.
He was *talked down* by a dispatcher who stayed on the line for an hour.

ru: сбивать, сбить (цену); уговаривать, уговорить снизить цену
separable: separable — *talk down the price*, *talk the price down*, *talk him down to four hundred*; never ✗ *talk down him*.
gloss: To persuade a seller to accept a lower price.
examples: I *talked* the dealer *down* to nine thousand.
You can usually *talk down* the asking price on a used bike.
She is very good at *talking* landlords *down* a hundred dollars a month.

ru: обсуждать, обсудить до конца; выяснять, выяснить отношения; проговаривать, проговорить
separable: separable — *talk out the problem*, *talk the problem out*; with a pronoun it must split, and *talk it out* is the commonest form of all.
gloss: To discuss a problem thoroughly until it is settled.
examples: They sat on the porch and *talked* the whole thing *out*.
It's better to *talk it out* than to trade angry texts.
We've been *talking out* the details all week.

ru: пользоваться, воспользоваться (в своих интересах); спекулировать (на чём-л.)
separable: inseparable — *trade on his reputation*, never ✗ *trade his reputation on*.
gloss: To use something, often unfairly, to get an advantage for yourself.
examples: He *trades on* his father's name every chance he gets.
The company *traded on* its reputation long after the quality slipped.
She got the job without *trading on* anyone's connections.

separable: separable — *trick out the truck*, *trick the truck out*, *trick it out*; never ✗ *trick out it*. The participle is very common as an adjective: *a tricked-out van*.
gloss: To fit something out with a lot of showy extras.
examples: He *tricked out* his pickup with light bars and chrome.
They *trick* these vans *out* for weekend camping.
The studio came *tricked out* with gear he never once used.

separable: inseparable — *wait on customers*, *wait on tables*, never ✗ *wait customers on*.
gloss: To serve food and drinks to customers, or to look after someone's every need.
examples: The same server *waits on* us every Sunday.
She *waited on* tables for six years to pay for school.
He has been *waiting on* the corner booth all night.

separable: inseparable — *wait on the results*, never ✗ *wait the results on*. In American English this is interchangeable with *wait for* when you are waiting for something to arrive or happen.
gloss: To wait for something or someone to arrive or to happen.
examples: We're still *waiting on* the lab results.
I *waited on* him for forty minutes outside the theater.
Half the office *waits on* one slow printer.

ru: уходить, уйти (от проблемы); бросать, бросить; отказываться, отказаться
separable: no object — intransitive; what you leave behind follows *from*: *walk away from the deal*.
gloss: To leave a difficult situation or relationship instead of dealing with it.
examples: Sometimes the smart move is to *walk away*.
He *walked away* from a twelve-year marriage and never explained why.
She's *walking away* from the offer even though the money is good.

ru: попадать, попасть (в ловушку); нарываться, нарваться; влипать, влипнуть
separable: inseparable — *walk into a trap*, never ✗ *walk a trap into*. Often strengthened with *right* or *straight*: *walked right into it*.
gloss: To get yourself into a bad situation without seeing it coming.
examples: He *walked into* an ambush of reporters outside the courthouse.
Ask him that and you'll *walk into* a lecture about taxes.
She had no idea what she was *walking into* when she took the job.

separable: no object — intransitive; what you escape follows *of*: *weasel out of the contract*.
gloss: To avoid a duty or a promise by being dishonest or too clever.
examples: He *weaseled out* of paying his share again.
Don't try to *weasel out* of it now.
She's always *weaseling out* of the early shift.

ru: смотреть сквозь пальцы (на что-л.); закрывать, закрыть глаза (на что-л.)
separable: inseparable — *wink at the violations*, never ✗ *wink the violations at*.
gloss: To pretend not to notice something wrong so that it can go on.
examples: Inspectors *winked at* the violations for years.
A city that *winks at* bad landlords ends up with bad housing.
The firm was accused of *winking at* cheating on the trading floor.

ru: желать, пожелать (кому-л. чего-л. плохого); навязывать, навязать (кому-л.)
separable: always split — the thing comes first and the person follows *on*: *wish that job on somebody*, never ✗ *wish on somebody that job*. The everyday frame is *I wouldn't wish it on my worst enemy*.
gloss: To want something bad to happen to someone, or to push something unwanted onto them.
examples: I wouldn't *wish* that commute *on* my worst enemy.
They *wished* their broken copier *on* the new branch.
He spends his evenings *wishing* his own bad luck *on* everybody else.

separable: inseparable — *work on the car*, never ✗ *work the car on*.
gloss: To spend time repairing something or making it better.
examples: I need to *work on* my Spanish before the trip.
He *worked on* that engine every weekend all winter.
She's been *working on* the same chapter since March.

separable: inseparable — the person follows the particle: *work on him*, never ✗ *work him on*.
gloss: To keep trying to persuade someone to change their mind.
examples: He doesn't want to come, but I'm *working on* him.
The lobbyists *worked on* two senators for a month.
She has *worked on* her parents since the day the brochure arrived.

separable: separable — *work over the witness*, *work the witness over*; with a pronoun it must split: *work him over*, never ✗ *work over him*.
gloss: To beat someone up badly.
examples: Two guys *worked* him *over* in the parking lot.
They threatened to *work over* anyone who talked to the police.
He came back looking like somebody had *worked* him *over*.
